To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) fuzzy regions can be represented by means of fuzzy sets over the plane, and (b) the metric operations on fuzzy regions are defined in terms of the fuzzy set operations.
Metric operations on fuzzy regions and fuzzy linear segments are defined and implemented.
the fuzzy spatial objects can be defined as fuzzy regions and fuzzy curves.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: - the definition of fuzzy spatial data types for representing spatial phenomena with indeterminate boundaries - the design of metric operations for these fuzzy spatial data types - the development of a fuzzy spatial query language - the implementation of a prototype system for fuzzy spatial data types and operations
the design of a data model for spatial objects with fuzzy boundaries and with the implementation of a fuzzy spatial object algebra.
the design and implementation of an efficient fuzzy spatial data type and the definition of a calculus of fuzzy spatial objects in a database.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fuzzy spatial model and the fuzzy metric operations on it are well suited for modeling and querying the spatial data in many real-world applications.

the metric operations on fuzzy regions and fuzzy line segments can be defined by using the fuzzy metric operations on crisp regions and crisp line segments, but with the additional requirement that the fuzzy metric operations are applied to all the crisp regions and crisp segments involved.
metric operations on fuzzy spatial regions and lines are possible and can be efficiently implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an algebra for metric operations on fuzzy spatial data, which is a first step towards a fuzzy spatial data model for databases.
we have shown that metric operations on fuzzy spatial data are possible, and we have provided a set of such operations for fuzzy spatial objects.
we provide an algebraic framework for metric operations on fuzzy spatial regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vagueness of the data can be modeled in a way that is both intuitive and computationally feasible.
metric operations can be extended to fuzzy objects, and that the extension is in many cases very simple, and can be performed in a way that is very close to the classical metric operations.
metric operations can be implemented on fuzzy spatial objects by means of fuzzy spatial operations on the corresponding crisp spatial objects.
